Follow-up 4 months.

documents.title: Dermatology return visit
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dermatology - return visit

Known to us from tinea pedis last fall. Has schizophrenia, diabetes and obesity.

Two weeks of an itchy rash on his trunk. It started as one small red patch and has gradually spread outward. No new medications. No recent travel. No known allergies.

Meds: risperidone, metformin, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, atenolol.

Exam: On the back, a well-demarcated erythematous annular plaque with a raised, scaly advancing edge and central clearing. Smaller similar annular lesions on both forearms. Toe webs clear.

KOH from the active border: septate hyphae.

Recent labs from his primary care office: fasting glucose 146, hemoglobin A1c 7.2%, CBC within normal limits, HIV test negative.

Assessment: tinea corporis.

Plan: ketoconazole 2% cream twice daily to the back and forearm lesions for 3 weeks. Launder towels and work clothes separately, keep using shower sandals. Follow up if not clearing.

Dermatology

events.reason: Episodes of upward eye deviation and neck twisting

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 7 days

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE

CC: eyes rolling up, neck twisting

HPI: 35-year-old man with schizophrenia, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, CKD and obesity, followed regularly by his PCP (history includes insulin resistance, a resected pheochromocytoma, pseudogynecomastia and tinea infections). His psychiatrist increased his risperidone four days ago. Today he has had several sudden spells in which both eyes lock upward, each lasting as long as an hour, with his neck and trunk pulled into a twisted posture. Between spells he is awake, alert and without fever. No eye injury or eye surgery. Denies seeing things that aren't there and denies any change in his vision.

Medications: risperidone (dose recently raised), metformin 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atenolol 50 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
SH: never smoker, social alcohol, warehouse associate.
Family: schizophrenia in maternal uncle, diabetes in father, hypertension in mother.

Exam: Vitals as recorded, afebrile. During an episode: sustained upward gaze of both eyes with torticollis. Face without rash; conjunctivae not injected; no eyelid swelling. Between spasms neurologic exam is otherwise normal - no tremor, no clonus, no rigidity.

ED course: Benztropine 2 mg IV at 20:05; episode resolved within about 20 minutes and none recurred during 3 hours of observation.

Impression: Oculogyric crisis - acute dystonic reaction to recent risperidone dose increase.

Disposition: Discharged home. Benztropine 1 mg by mouth twice daily for 7 days. Call psychiatry tomorrow regarding the dose. Follow up with PCP this week. Return for recurrence not relieved by benztropine, fever, stiffness or confusion.

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 2 days after ED visit for oculogyric crisis.

His psychiatrist raised risperidone from 2 mg to 3 mg twice daily on 10/4. On 10/8 he had repeated episodes of eyes locking upward with neck twisting, treated with IV benztropine in the ED with prompt relief. Since then none. Taking benztropine 1 mg BID as directed, through Monday. Spoke with psychiatry yesterday; he says they plan to keep the 3 mg. Mild worry about it happening again at work.

Vitals as charted.
Calm, conversant. Eyes: full extraocular movements, no deviation. Neck: full range, no spasm. Neuro: no tremor, normal tone, normal gait.

A/P
1. Oculogyric crisis from risperidone increase - resolved, on short benztropine course. Med list updated to risperidone 3 mg BID. If any recurrence: benztropine and call psychiatry same day / ED.
2. Flu vaccine today (he agreed this year).
3. DM/HTN follow-up December as planned.

documents.title: Psychiatry note
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Re: ED visit 10/8 for acute dystonia (oculogyric crisis). Risperidone had been increased to 3 mg twice daily on 10/4 for better control of his psychotic symptoms. After discussion with Mr. Reyes we are continuing 3 mg twice daily, as the dystonia responded fully to benztropine. Benztropine 1 mg twice daily for the 7-day course only, no ongoing anticholinergic planned. He will contact us immediately with any recurrence. Next visit in 3 weeks.
